title: Mediations Handled by Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management
what_it_is: Mediations Handled by Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management

sections.label: TADM mediation of salary claims
sections.summary: Between April and December 2017, TADM concluded mediation for 6,000 salary-related claims, with 79% settled amicably, 12% unsettled and 9% involving non-attendance.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Between April and December 2017, TADM concluded mediation for 6,000 salary-related claims under ECA.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Seventy-nine percent of these 6,000 claims were settled amicably through mediation.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Twelve percent were not settled as parties were unable to work out a settlement.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: The remaining 9% were claims involving non-attendance at mediation, in other words, someone did not show up.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: For the remaining two-thirds, when respondents did not attend mediation, claimants could have their claims heard and adjudicated by the ECTs, even if respondents do not turn up for the hearing.

sections.label: Salary recovery by TADM and tribunal
sections.summary: TADM and the tribunal have helped about 92% of employees with valid salary claims recover their salaries in full.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: To date, TADM and the tribunal have helped about 92% of employees with valid salary claims recover their salaries in full.

sections.label: No cap on claims filed
sections.summary: There is no cap on claims that can be filed, and a respondent's non-attendance does not prevent the tribunal from awarding full payment on a valid claim.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In answer to the first question, I stand corrected, but there is no cap to the claims that can be filed.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To the second question, as I said in my earlier reply, even if the respondent does not turn up, it does not prevent the claimant from bringing the matter to the tribunal, and the tribunal will look at the validity of the claims and, if the tribunal is convinced that the claimant has filed a valid claim, then the fact that the respondent did not show up at the hearing does not prevent the tribunal from awarding full payment as claimed to the claimant.
